targetText: From all that has been said in this book on the economic essence of imperialism, it follows that we must define it as capitalism in transition, or, more precisely, as moribund capitalism.
summary: Imperialism is decaying, moribund capitalism: the final transitional stage where corporate concentration and socialized production set the stage for a planned socialist economy.
context: Monopoly capitalism organizes production on a massive, global scale. All that remains is to transfer ownership of these socialized industries from private monopolists to society as a whole.

targetText: when a single centre directs all the consecutive stages of processing the material
summary: Monopoly corporations create vast planned supply chains that integrate raw materials, manufacturing, and distribution under single administrative systems.
context: Capitalism ironically creates global economic planning within giant corporations (like modern global supply networks), proving that large-scale economic planning is practical and efficient.

targetText: The most dangerous of all in this respect are those who do not wish to understand that the fight against imperialism is a sham and humbug unless it is inseparably bound up with the fight against opportunism.
summary: Opposing imperialism is impossible without simultaneously struggling against reformist political leaders who compromise with financial monopolies and defend imperialist wars.
context: Lenin stresses that working-class movements cannot succeed if their leaders accept crumbs from imperial superprofits and support national corporate interests over global solidarity.
